topic: Type-safe Bitwise Flag Operations Using Enum Classes
explanation: In modern C++, enum classes (scoped enumerations) are used to define strongly typed, scoped constants, including flags for bitwise operations. Unlike traditional enums, enum classes prevent implicit conversions to integers, enhancing type safety. When representing multiple options or flags (such as file open modes), combining enum class values with bitwise operators requires explicit operator overloading to ensure clarity and correctness. This approach improves code safety and readability by avoiding accidental misuse of bitwise operations on unrelated types.
